title: Welcome to My Household
primary_topics: Welcome remarks at CJP's Makati home for a courtesy call by Singapore CJ Sundaresh Menon and an 11-person Singapore delegation on April 12, 2019 -- the day before the AsnLI inaugural

Introduction of CJP's household: Leni (Chinese paintings displayed throughout the living room), five children (two in Philippines, three in US), two Manila-based grandchildren (Rafa at Ateneo, Miguel finishing Babson MBA)

Introduction of ALA Philippines' major supporters: Tessie Sy-Coson (P6 million donation; former CJP student), James Go (JG Summit), Manny Pangilinan (PLDT, Meralco, MPIC), and Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala (Ayala Corporation; absent, abroad)
Introduction of the ALA Philippines National Committee to CJ Menon -- the specific purpose of the home visit requested by the Singapore delegation
sub_topics: CJP's surprise and humility at being visited by CJ Menon: 'I was so surprised and honored... I did not think that I, in particular, deserve it. After all, I have already retired from active service and have passed my prime while Your Honor is the distinguished head of the Singapore judiciary'

CJP's invitation for Menon and the delegation to tour his home: the den (manuscripts of the 1,200 decisions he penned + 14 books), the memorabilia room (souvenirs, honorary doctoral degree gowns, desk and furniture purchased from the Supreme Court) -- 'They should really be in a museum. Unfortunately, the Supreme Court does not have one'
Justice Chao Hick Tin's prior courtesy: when CJP was incumbent CJ, Justice Chao (then ALA President) flew to the Philippines and honored him with a 'big celebration at the nearby Dusit Thane Hotel'
Leni's Chinese paintings: after retiring from AIM in 2009, Leni learned Chinese painting; all around the living room are her works; the delegation receives smaller reprints as keepsake gifts

Miggy Sandejas: eldest grandson; finishing Masters in Entrepreneurship at Babson College, Boston; CJP's joke -- Miggy didn't need to go to Babson, he should have applied as assistant to Tessie Sy-Coson 'the charming Chairman of BDO, the largest bank in the Philippines' who 'according to Forbes, is the richest woman in our country'

Tessie Sy-Coson: major ALA Philippines supporter; donated P6 million two years ago (source of the $100,000 AsnLI seed money); CJP's former student in commercial law 'about 10 years ago when she was still a teenager taking up her Bachelor of Commerce degree at the nearby Assumption College'; her father Henry Sy -- 'the richest man in our country until his death earlier this year' -- stopped her from becoming a lawyer; 'Now, she can retain the world's best and brightest lawyers -- with her as the boss'
James Go: JG Summit chairman; owns Cebu Pacific Air, food and beverage, petrochemicals, big real estate company, second largest super malls chain
Manny Pangilinan: PLDT, Meralco, MPIC (water distribution, tollways, power generation, 14 hospitals in partnership with GIC of Singapore, logistics, railways, and other businesses)

ALA Philippines National Committee: Justices Carpio and Reyes Jr. (present); Justice Bernabe (abroad); Ave Cruz; Alfredo C. Lim (PAGCOR President); Danilo Concepcion (UP President); absentees: Senator Franklin Drilon, Emilio Aquino (SEC Chairman), former ALA Secretary General Gina Geraldez, Jerry Parulan; honorary chairman CJ Bersamin (out of town, returning tonight)

ALA Philippines officers: Grace Salonga, Andre Palacios (new AsnLI Director General), Rowena Flores, Maria Teresita Sison Go, Sol Hermosura, Mike Toledo, Gov. Boy Reyno, Dr. Sam Bernal (three earned doctorates -- LL.D., M.D., Ph.D. -- plus finishing a Doctor of Chemistry), Executive Assistant Marivic Romualdez

stances.claim: CJP's 1,200 SC decisions, 14 books, memorabilia (gowns, desk, furniture purchased from the SC) should be in a museum -- 'Unfortunately, the Supreme Court does not have one.' This passing remark presages the FLP Museum for Liberty and Prosperity project, and frames the home as an improvisational institutional memory keeper.
stances.rhetorical_move: museum-gap argument: the absence of an SC museum is a national institutional deficit, not just a personal inconvenience
stances.confidence: asserted as an observation that many retired colleagues share

stances.claim: Tessie Sy-Coson's trajectory -- from CJP's commercial law student who wanted to be a lawyer but was redirected by father Henry Sy into entrepreneurship -- is now complete: 'She can retain the world's best and brightest lawyers -- with her as the boss.' The lawyer-as-student became the entrepreneur-as-commander, vindicating both paths.
stances.rhetorical_move: student-to-boss inversion as the ultimate tribute to both entrepreneurship and legal education
stances.confidence: asserted with gentle wit as a personal observation

notable_anecdotes: Leni's Chinese paintings: after retiring from AIM in 2009, Leni learned Chinese painting; all around the living room are her works. The Singapore delegation receives smaller reprints as keepsake gifts.

The SC museum-gap: CJP's den contains manuscripts of 1,200 decisions and 14 books; the memorabilia room holds souvenirs, honorary degree gowns, and the desk and furniture he purchased from the SC. 'They should really be in a museum. Unfortunately, the Supreme Court does not have one. Many of my retired colleagues are urging me to spearhead a private funding for such a museum, but that's quite another story.'

Tessie Sy-Coson's story: Henry Sy -- 'until his death earlier this year' (January 2019) the richest man in the Philippines -- stopped his daughter from becoming a lawyer and asked her to be an entrepreneur instead. CJP: 'Now, she can retain the world's best and brightest lawyers -- with her as the boss.'

Dr. Sam Bernal's multiple doctorates: among the ALA Philippines officers introduced, Dr. Sam Bernal 'holds three earned doctorates, Doctor of Laws, Doctor of Medicine, Doctor of Philosophy and is now finishing his Doctor of Chemistry.' Presented deadpan as a single compound sentence.

Miggy's Babson joke: 'I told Miguel that to be a great entrepreneur, he did not have to go to [Babson]. He should have just applied as an assistant or messenger of one of our special guests today, Ms Tessie Sy-Coson.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered April 12, 2019 at CJP's Makati home during a courtesy call by Singapore CJ Sundaresh Menon and 11 justices and lawyers -- the day before the AsnLI inaugural -- this welcome address opens with CJP expressing genuine surprise and humility at being visited ('I did not think that I, in particular, deserve it... I have already retired from active service and have passed my prime'), inviting the delegation to tour his den (manuscripts of the 1,200 decisions he penned + 14 books) and memorabilia room (souvenirs, honorary doctoral degree gowns, and the desk and furniture he purchased from the SC -- 'They should really be in a museum; unfortunately, the Supreme Court does not have one'). He recalls Justice Chao's prior courtesy when Chao was ALA President and CJP was incumbent CJ -- 'I will never forget the honor you bestowed on me as long as I live.' He introduces Leni (retired from AIM in 2009, now a Chinese painting artist whose works fill the living room, with smaller reprints given as keepsake gifts), and notes that daughter Tet is away hosting a reception for her own daughter, while daughter Len and husband Alex are present; grandson Rafa is at school at Ateneo; grandson Miggy is finishing his Babson MBA in Boston. He introduces the ALA Philippines business supporters: Tessie Sy-Coson (P6 million ALA donor, BDO Chairman, 'according to Forbes the richest woman in our country,' and CJP's former student in commercial law at Assumption College when her father Henry Sy -- 'until his death earlier this year the richest man in our country' -- stopped her from becoming a lawyer; 'Now, she can retain the world's best and brightest lawyers -- with her as the boss'); James Go (JG Summit); and Manny Pangilinan (PLDT, Meralco, MPIC). He then presents the ALA Philippines National Committee, including Justices Carpio and Reyes Jr., Ave Cruz, PAGCOR President Alfredo Lim, UP President Danilo Concepcion, and the ALA Philippines officers -- ending with Dr. Sam Bernal ('three earned doctorates -- Doctor of Laws, Doctor of Medicine, Doctor of Philosophy -- and now finishing his Doctor of Chemistry').
